prompt: Implement glob matching where * stands for any run of characters and ? for exactly one, then use it to filter a list of names. Complete matches and filter, then run the tests.
explanation: A boolean table ok[i][j] answers "do the first i pattern characters match the first j text characters?", which turns the tricky backtracking of * into a simple two-loop fill. A star either consumes nothing (ok[i-1][j]) or swallows one more text character (ok[i][j-1]); a ? or a literal match only extends the diagonal cell. Seeding column 0 with leading stars is what lets "*" match the empty string, and reading ok[n][m] enforces that the whole text was consumed.
hints: Make a boolean[pattern.length() + 1][text.length() + 1] where cell [i][j] means "pattern prefix of length i matches text prefix of length j". Cell [0][0] is true.
Column 0 (empty text) is true only while every pattern character so far is '*'.
For '*': ok[i][j] = ok[i-1][j] || ok[i][j-1]. For '?' or a matching literal: ok[i][j] = ok[i-1][j-1]. Everything else stays false.
